absent: Scheduling triggers, queuing sites, and cancellation rules for discard and reclamation work.
Complete field order, offsets, sizes, and alignment for device, cluster, extent, and entry structures.
Numeric values and full semantics for cluster sizing, table encoding, and count maximum constants.
Full traversal completion for address space reclamation beyond the truncated range handler.
Device lifetime, reference counting, and teardown sequencing for swap devices.
Swap cache insertion, lookup, removal, and readahead interaction details.
Backing block mapping for multi extent devices beyond single extent translation shown.
Architecture specific restoration and page table helper semantics.
Exact error code taxonomy for all failure paths beyond the observed invalid, memory, busy, missing, and unsupported cases.
Processor local cluster initialization, migration, and teardown.
Use of the latency bound constant in control flow.

findings.text: A swap related latency bound constant carries value 256.
Duplication of swap references for a folio is offered, handling either an entire folio or a single page within it, with a requirement that the caller hold the folio locked and cached.

Release of swap references for a folio is offered, handling either an entire folio or a single page within it, with a requirement that the caller hold the folio locked and cached, and without triggering cache reclamation from this path.

Queries expose how many references exist for a swap entry, whether any reference exists, and a device pinned count that resolves overflow storage, with unlocked, cluster locked, and device pinned variants.
Direct release of a contiguous run of swap entries is offered, splitting the run at cluster boundaries and invoking cache reclamation for affected clusters.
A retry helper for overflow storage allocation is offered, resolving the device and cluster for an entry and attempting allocation with caller supplied allocation flags.

Hibernation slot management is offered, allocating a single entry from a given swap type and freeing a single entry while deferring deallocation for cached content and attempting opportunistic cache reclamation.

Hibernation device selection is offered through lookup by block device and offset, pinning with exclusive flag protection against concurrent or repeated use, unpinning, and retrieval of the first usable device.

Device queries are offered, translating a type plus offset into a backing block location only when the device is writable, and reporting total or free page counts for a type under appropriate locking.

Asynchronous handlers are provided for scheduled discard, full cluster reclamation, reference release completion, and deferred table folio release, each resolving its enclosing device or folio from the callback context.

Discard processing excludes the header page from the first extent while covering whole subsequent extents, converting page counts to block counts, yielding between extents, and propagating the first failure with unsupported operation as a common outcome.

Bad slot marking respects a possibly shrunken usable maximum, adjusts the usable page tally except for the header and masking cases, rejects empty devices and duplicated markings, ensures table presence before update, and validates cluster tallies and flags.

Overflow storage for highly shared slots is allocated optimistically and installed only when still required, with revalidation for concurrent installation, loss of allocation need, or freed state, and is released when no overflow entries remain.

Reference count adjustments distinguish inline tallies from overflow storage, reject invalid transitions involving bad or unreferenced slots, and trigger overflow allocation or release around threshold crossings.

Release of multiple entries within a cluster batches consecutive releasable slots for efficient freeing, defers cached entries until cache departure, and optionally attempts reclamation of newly unmapped cache content.

Duplication of multiple entries within a cluster provides atomicity through rollback of already duplicated entries on failure, releasing the cluster lock to allow overflow allocation before retrying the failed slot.
Hibernation allocation favors the processor local cluster when it belongs to the requested device and remains usable, otherwise falling back to general cluster allocation.
Hibernation device lookup requires a valid block identity, scans only writable devices, and matches both the device identity and the starting backing location of the first extent.

Restoration of a swapped mapping validates cache association, handles copy on sharing and poisoned content with distinct swap markers, maintains anonymous and swap occupancy tallies, preserves soft dirty and fault handling attributes, and defers arch specific restoration before reference release.

Reclamation of a swap type walks address spaces hierarchically, filtering for relevant swap entries, obtaining cached content or reading ahead on miss, skipping already unreferenced entries on allocation failure, and serializing each mapping restoration with locking and writeback waiting.
Comparison of a page table entry against a swap entry ignores volatile swap flags to test underlying equality.

Per cluster serialization guards the small table, usage tally, flags, and optional overflow storage, held across reference adjustments and freeing, released temporarily for blocking overflow allocation, with debug assertions requiring held state in low level helpers.

Global swap serialization guards the device table, type lookup, and hibernation flag updates, nesting outside per device serialization for page accounting, while hibernation allocation uses processor local serialization and mapping restoration uses page table serialization.

Observed device state includes a backing device, usable maximum and page tally, type identifier, status flags, extent list, cluster array, and work items for discard and reclamation; observed cluster state includes a lock, usage tally, flags, small table, and optional overflow array; observed extent state includes start location and length in both block and page units.

A swap slot moves among unallocated, bad, counted, overflow counted, and cached combinations, with overflow engaged near the inline maximum and cached status preventing freeing until cache exit, and with failed multi duplication returning to the prior state via rollback.

Hibernation device pinning moves from unpinned to pinned under global serialization, rejecting repeated pinning as busy, and returns to unpinned on explicit release, with lookup and allocation valid only for writable pinned candidates.

Failure modes include unsupported discard, empty device on bad marking, duplicated bad markings, overflow allocation exhaustion with retry, invalid reference transitions, out of range direct release, missing device on hibernation paths, and poisoned or writeback content during mapping restoration.

Concurrency hazards include concurrent overflow installation and release requiring revalidation, readahead insertion racing with hibernation release, cache removal racing with mapping restoration, and lock release during allocation requiring restart of duplication.
